status: Accepted causal historical reproduction and isolated scoped-lifetime differential; original failure retained

historical_failure.observed: Sync consumer previously read fourteen records and reported assignment partition zero. Several blocking metadata/group/time calls intervened before seek returned State. The other four seek cases were skipped by the group dependency.
historical_failure.native_diagnosis: At native release 2.15.0 rd_kafka_seek waits for the fetcher result. rd_kafka_toppar_seek returns State for a fetch state below OFFSET_QUERY, excluding STOPPING, which returns PrevInProgress. Thus the assignment snapshot did not establish the later active-fetcher precondition.
historical_failure.limit: The saved log alone does not identify the native transition. The new native-only reproduction shows duplicate topic/partition identity; parent lifetime and late finalizer ordering are under investigation. No max-poll or broker event is asserted as the cause.

fixture_change: All five inherited positive offset scenarios run in both modes on fresh run-owned topics and unique grouped consumers. Each confirms exact record zero immediately before seeking, then verifies exact next identity/offset/value or documented EOF/timeout. Unassignment/State/reassignment and repeated replay remain separate tests. State is not suppressed or retried into success.

rejected_hypothesis.description: A deliberately short max-poll interval produced MAXPOLL and a stale assignment query, but seek still succeeded. This does not reproduce or explain the historical trigger.

scope_decision.completion_requirement: Identify a reproducible supported transition that accounts for the saved condition, with concrete native/operation evidence; passing reruns and an unknown-cause limitation do not close this requirement.

continued_forensics.archive_crosscheck: Historical mutation archive retains byte-identical ConsumerTest.hs, TestEnv.hs, Consumer.hs and ConsumerProperties.hs relative to fc5892d. The native/admin source hashes also match the preserved subject manifest. The whole failed-run fingerprint differs, so no exact whole-candidate reconstruction is claimed.

traced_replay.result: pass; sync fetcher remains active through metadata/group/time queries and first seek is served in active state

forced_gc_replay.result: pass with explicit performGC before every inherited consumer operation; not a reconstruction

continued_forensics.broker_log: Read-only retained primary broker logs establish the exact historical topic was created at 2026-10-24 07:33:31.078 UTC and deleted at 07:34:47.721 UTC after the suite teardown. No intervening deletion of that exact topic occurs. Default INFO logs contain no matching group/fetch-state transition, so they cannot identify the inactive-fetcher cause.
continued_forensics.accepted_cause: A managed legacy-seek topic may outlive its native client. Its late C finalizer accesses the freed parent; when that address is reused by the next consumer, TAILQ_REMOVE writes through the old topic link into the new client topic-list head. Metadata/name lookup then constructs a second topic/partition in fetch state none while the real assigned partition remains active. Legacy seek resolves that second partition and returns State.

native_trace_reproduction.status: Native State reproduced; exact object divergence under investigation
native_trace_reproduction.native_change: C-only fetch-state transitions and seek-entry trace, with stop-state backtraces; no behavior/layout change. ConsumerTest restored to original with no Haskell debug or forced GC.
native_trace_reproduction.observed: Consumer 73 delivers records on an active partition; first seek later enters with state none. No active-to-none transition is logged; the original active partition reaches stopping/stopped only during final teardown. Distinguish object identity before attributing the result to lost assignment or a stopped fetcher.

identity_probe.observed: The reproduced failing sync consumer delivers on rkt 0xba7a2c500 / partition 0xba7328500. During all-topics metadata a second rkt 0xba7a2ca00 / partition 0xba7328f00 is created for the same topic. Seek uses the second partition in state none. The original remains active until teardown. A separate native lifetime trace aborts when the preceding async consumer topic finalizer accesses its already destroyed parent mutex; parent-address reuse is under investigation.
identity_probe.limit: Do not yet assert that the precise old saved event was a late finalizer. The observed duplicate object and separate invalid-parent destructor motivate a direct address/order probe.

causal_acceptance.historical_subject: fc5892d core Consumer/Metadata/native API sources with original ConsumerTest and GHC coverage; no Haskell debug/forced GC in the reproducing run. Core source bytes match the original preserved mutation archive; whole failed-candidate fingerprint was not reconstructable.
causal_acceptance.native_trace: Tagged librdkafka 2.15.0 with C-only pointer/state/finalizer logging; no native behavior or opaque layout change.
timeline: Async consumer 72 uses parent 0xbff0b8000, topic 0xbfee2de00 and active partition 0xbfee2e800.
Sync consumer 73 reuses native parent address 0xbff0b8000 and delivers fourteen records using a different topic 0xbfee2e800 and partition 0xbfee2d900.
During watermark lookup two delayed application-reference releases finalize old topic 0xbfee2de00. Its parent now reports consumer-73; the stack is runSomeFinalizers -> rd_kafka_topic_destroy_final.
Native by-name lookup now reports topic count zero, while the original assigned partition has not stopped.
Metadata/topic lookup constructs topic 0xbfee2de00 again with a new never-started partition 0xbfee2ca00. Seek enters that partition in state none and returns State; four dependent cases skip.

A separate explicit client-lifetime trace, with no address reuse, records destruction/free of parent consumer 72 before its topic finalizer and aborts on the destroyed parent mutex. This corroborates the invalid lifetime independently of topic-list corruption.

minimal_differential.change: Only legacy seek in the historical checkout is changed to retain its parent with withForeignPtr and bracket/finalize every acquired topic before returning, mirroring the already implemented current lifetime fix. No offsets, errors, waits, topic fixtures or callback mode is changed.
minimal_differential.finalizer_order: Both historical consumer topics finalize while their original parent is still alive; no State and no duplicate topic object.

current_repair.behavior: Legacy seek retains the native client and explicitly finalizes scoped topics; current native-child Haskell finalizers also retain the parent. Existing ten fresh positive scenarios, native State propagation/recovery tests, full primary normal/mapped runs and current native diagnostic cohorts remain accepted.

causal_acceptance.scope_limit: This is a causal reproduction of the saved failure condition with the preserved historical core, not a claim that the untraced original process event can be observed retrospectively. The stopped-fetcher and max-poll explanations are not asserted.
